minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to support a skate park within Marshall Park; size and exact location remain open.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the skate park group's slide presentation comparing Marshall Park with the TC Passios site, then discussed pros, cons, size, safety and grants. A motion to support a skate park within Marshall Park was taken by roll call. The group will confer and return, and a size discussion was scheduled for the next meeting.

public_comment.topic: Skate park group spokesperson introduced the group and the presentation, noting the project began over three years ago.
Presented why the town needs a skate park, fundraising and site pros and cons.
Parent supported collaboration between the skate park group and the commission and commended both sides.
Resident gave history of skating and the failed earlier park, and suspected objections to the TC Passios site came from nearby town hall and Eagle House users.
Skate park board member argued the park will become a destination regardless of site.
Asked for a prompt follow-up meeting so the group and commission can reach consensus on size and location.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park grants and open space plan
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission has a promised collaboration with the open space committee to help with grants, and the skate park could fold into the overall funding.
A member asked for a future agenda item on the revolving fund before the warrant closes.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted 4-0 on a roll call to support building a skate park within Marshall Park.
The vote leaves the skate park's size and exact location within Marshall Park undecided; size, including an earlier 5,000 square foot position, is to be discussed later.
The skate park group presented slides comparing Marshall Park with the TC Passios site, and the commission discussed pros, cons, safety and grants.
The chair offered the group a 30 to 45 minute slot at the February 12 meeting, and the group is to say by the eighth or ninth whether it wants it.
A member asked that a decision on the park revolving fund go on the next agenda, before the spring town meeting warrant closes.

why_it_matters: The vote points the skate park toward land the town already treats as park, where grants are available, rather than the TC Passios lot, where grants are likely not.
Size and exact placement are still open, and those details will shape how much the project costs and how much private fundraising versus public money it needs.
The revolving fund item is timed to the spring town meeting warrant, so any article touching park funds would reach voters then.

Next agenda: park revolving fund decision, before the spring town meeting warrant closes.
